steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Context: After Pope Pius V excommunicated Elizabeth in 1570, Catholic plots to overthrow her intensified. Mary Queen of Scots, Elizabeth's Catholic cousin, was the focal point of every conspiracy - she was the obvious Catholic alternative to Elizabeth. Elizabeth's survival depended on her spy network, led by Francis Walsingham, and her ability to outmanoeuvre the plotters without provoking an international crisis. | Significance of the Revolt: The Revolt of the Northern Earls was the only armed Catholic uprising of Elizabeth's reign. It showed that Catholic nobles in the north were willing to use force, but it also demonstrated the limits of their support. Most ordinary people, even Catholics, were unwilling to risk their lives for the cause. The revolt's failure strengthened Elizabeth

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe the Revolt of the Northern Earls in 1569. (4 marks) | Explain how Walsingham's spy network uncovered the Babington Plot. (4 marks) | Why did Elizabeth hesitate before signing Mary Queen of Scots' death warrant? (4 marks)

steps.title: Homework & Consolidation
steps.body: Consolidation, retrieval on Key Context, Significance of the Revolt, Walsingham's Spy Network, and one past-paper question.
